## Week-by-week approximate schedule

### Week 1 (August 24-28) - Why databases?

Introduce spreadsheets, files, and databases as different tools for different problems. Focus on repeated information, hidden assumptions, naive tabular representations, and why data integrity becomes hard to maintain.

### Week 2 (August 31-September 4) - Relational foundations and query implementation

Introduce the relational model, core terminology, keys, and the idea of data independence. Develop relational algebra as a formal language for query meaning, introduce Assignment 1, and use class time to implement basic relational operations in Python.

### Week 3 (September 7-11) - PostgreSQL table definitions and SQL foundations

Begin by defining and changing PostgreSQL tables, then use basic SQL to query them. Develop joins, grouping, aggregation, set versus bag behavior, and query decomposition as the unit continues. No class Monday, September 7, because of Labor Day.

### Week 4 (September 14-18) - Query reasoning, equivalence, and first DataFrames

Compare equivalent query forms, logical query plans, and the difference between query meaning and execution strategy. Introduce a first comparison between SQL-style transformations and DataFrame-style transformations.

### Week 5 (September 21-25) - ER modeling foundations

Introduce entities, attributes, identifiers, relationships, cardinality, participation, and the role of assumptions in conceptual modeling.

### Week 6 (September 28-October 2) - ER modeling in depth

Extend ER modeling to weak and associative entities, recursive relationships, specialization/generalization, temporal requirements, and multivalued information.

### Week 7 (October 5-9) - From ER diagrams to relational schemas

Translate conceptual models into relations, keys, domain constraints, entity integrity, and referential integrity.

### Week 8 (October 12-16) - Dependencies and normalization

Introduce functional dependencies, candidate keys, anomalies, 3NF, BCNF, lossless decomposition, and dependency preservation. No class Monday, October 12, because of Indigenous Peoples' Day.

### Week 9 (October 19-23) - Review and midterm examination

Synthesize SQL, relational algebra, ER modeling, relational mapping, keys, constraints, dependencies, and normalization. Midterm examination: Friday, October 23, during the regular class meeting.

### Week 10 (October 26-30) - Advanced SQL

Develop common table expressions, window functions, conditional aggregation, views, and recursive queries as time permits.

### Week 11 (November 2-6) - Storage, indexes, and query plans

Introduce pages, records, B-trees, hashing, composite indexes, selectivity, scans, join algorithms, cardinality estimates, and plan choices.

### Week 12 (November 9-13) - Transactions and concurrency

Develop atomicity, isolation, consistency, durability, schedules, anomalies, serializability, isolation levels, locking, and MVCC. No class Wednesday, November 11, because of Veterans Day observed.

### Week 13 (November 16-20) - Analytical systems and cross-engine comparison

Compare OLTP and OLAP, row and column layouts, Parquet, DuckDB, Polars, projection/filter pushdown, and data-movement tradeoffs across systems.

### Week 14 (November 23-27) - Spatial database foundations

Introduce spatial types, geometry versus geography, coordinate reference systems, and spatial predicates. Instruction is limited this week because Wednesday, November 25 is a non-instructional travel day and November 26-27 is Thanksgiving holiday.

### Week 15 (November 30-December 4) - Spatial joins, integration, and review

Develop PostGIS spatial joins and indexes, selected broader database architectures, and final synthesis across correctness, query behavior, performance, and representation.

## Final examination

The cumulative final examination is worth 20% of the course grade. Its provisional date is **Wednesday, December 9, 2026**. The exact time must be aligned with the registrar's final-exam schedule after the regular meeting time is known.
